skill.name: agent-memory-systems
skill.description: Design agent memory systems that combine short-term context, long-term vector stores, retrieval strategy, chunking, metadata, decay, and conflict handling.
skill.summary: Guide AI agent memory architecture from storage design to retrieval quality.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Agents lose coherence when they cannot retrieve the right prior context. This skill guides memory architecture, chunking, retrieval, and decay choices for reliable long-term agent behavior.
actual_capabilities: Explains short-term, long-term, working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory patterns.
Guides vector store selection for different retrieval workloads.
Frames chunking strategy around retrievability and testing.
Highlights metadata filtering, temporal scoring, and embedding model tracking.
Identifies memory anti-patterns that reduce agent consistency.
limitations: Does not include executable implementation code or database adapters.
Does not benchmark vector databases or embedding models directly.
Requires users to test retrieval quality with their own data.
Does not replace privacy, retention, or compliance review for stored memories.

use_cases.title: Plan Memory Architecture
use_cases.description: Design how an agent stores, retrieves, updates, and expires memory across user sessions.

use_cases.title: Improve Retrieval Quality
use_cases.description: Review chunking, metadata filters, and temporal scoring when agents miss relevant context.

use_cases.title: Define Memory Evaluation
use_cases.description: Create practical checks for recall accuracy, conflict handling, and context budget use.

prompt_templates.title: Map Memory Needs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify the memory types my agent needs. Include short-term, long-term, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Retrieval Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for a knowledge-heavy agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a retrieval strategy for an agent that must answer from past conversations and documents. Include chunking, metadata, and ranking choices.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Forgetting
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting for inconsistent agent behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why my agent forgets important facts. Review storage, retrieval, context budget, memory decay, and conflict resolution risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for agent memory quality. Cover recall, precision, stale memory, conflicting memory, and token budget tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Design memory for a customer support agent.
output_examples.output: A layered memory plan with session context, customer profile facts, issue history, and retrieval filters by customer and recency.

output_examples.input: Review why an agent forgets document details.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis focused on chunk boundaries, missing metadata, weak embedding coverage, and no retrieval tests for expected questions.

output_examples.input: Plan memory decay for a coaching agent.
output_examples.output: A retention model that keeps stable user preferences, ages out transient goals, and flags contradictions before updating memory.

best_practices: Design retrieval before storage volume grows.
Test chunk sizes with real user questions.
Track source, timestamp, and embedding model metadata for each memory.
anti_patterns: Store every interaction forever without retention rules.
Use one memory type for all information.
Chunk documents without measuring whether answers can be retrieved.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps design memory systems that let agents retrieve useful prior context instead of only storing large amounts of data.

faq.question: Does it provide working code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, patterns, and review prompts for memory system design.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it only for vector databases?
faq.answer: No. It covers vector stores as one part of broader short-term, long-term, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory design.

faq.question: How should I validate a memory design?
faq.answer: Use representative questions to test recall, precision, chunk quality, metadata filters, decay rules, and conflict handling.

faq.question: Does it address privacy or compliance?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. Teams must still define retention, consent, access control, and deletion requirements for stored memories.
